findings.title: Moved log fields and new middleware have no tests
findings.description: The diff moves `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName` and `dsUID` out of `LoggerMiddleware`, which now emits only status, duration, eventName and time (logger_middleware.go:49-54). Those fields now come from `instrumentContext`, and reach the log line only through the context provider registered in `pkg/infra/log/log.go:55`. There is no `contextual_logger_middleware_test.go`. There is also no `logger_middleware_test.go`, so that gap predates this change. `metrics_middleware_test.go` only checks Prometheus output. A dropped field, a wrong key, or a reordered middleware list would ship without a failing test. Add a test that runs `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` and `NewLoggerMiddleware` with a logger that captures output. Note that `plog.TestLogger` cannot capture it (see the fake finding below).

findings.title: Field correctness depends on undocumented middleware order
findings.description: `LoggerMiddleware` now relies on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` running before it. The only thing enforcing that is list position in `CreateMiddlewares`. The order is correct today: `clientFromMiddlewares` reverses the list and wraps it, so the first entry is outermost (decorator.go:106-111). Nothing else documents or checks it. The rename also deleted the comment in `metrics_middleware.go` that stated stack placement. If someone reorders the list, or builds `NewLoggerMiddleware` in another chain, the "Plugin Request Completed" line silently loses its identifying fields and still reports success. Document the requirement next to `CreateMiddlewares`, or give the logger middleware an explicit contract.

findings.title: Shared mutable `next` in `MetricsMiddleware` is a data race
findings.description: `NewMetricsMiddleware` builds one `imw` and its closure writes `imw.next = next` (line 79) every time it runs. `Decorator` runs that closure on every request through `clientFromMiddlewares` (decorator.go:34, 48, 57, 66 and the other methods). Concurrent plugin requests therefore write and read `m.next` with no synchronization. Because the chains are structurally identical, the results are usually the same, but `-race` will flag it under concurrent load. This predates the diff, and the rename carries it forward. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (contextual_logger_middleware.go:14-19) avoids the pattern by allocating a fresh struct per call. Match that here while keeping the Prometheus registration to a single call.

findings.title: Test fake swallows calls made through `FromContext`
findings.description: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, so anything logged through the returned logger is recorded on a new fake, not the one the caller holds. `LoggerMiddleware` now emits its only log line via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go:58). A test that injects `plog.NewTestLogger()` and checks `InfoLogs.Calls` would see 0 and fail or pass for the wrong reason. `New` already has this pattern (fake.go:18-20), so it is a repo-wide habit, but this is the first call on the logging path to use it. Consider returning `f`, which keeps captured calls visible. The fake does not model context attributes anyway.

findings.title: Fallback branch in `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` is unreachable
findings.description: `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` always returns a `*ConcreteLogger` in its interface value (`cl` or `cl.New(...)`, log.go:203-217), and `d.l` is typed `*log.ConcreteLogger`. So the `ok` check at line 49 always succeeds and the `d.New()` fallback at lines 50-52 cannot run. Either assert directly or add a comment explaining why the check stays.

findings.title: Names not updated after the rename
findings.description: The test is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` after the file became `metrics_middleware_test.go`. The helper moved into `contextual_logger_middleware.go` still uses the name `instrumentContext` (line 27), though it no longer instruments metrics. Renaming both would make names match files and types.

findings.title: Unrelated `interface{}` to `any` churn in `ifaces.go`
findings.description: The `interface{}` to `any` changes across `Logger` and `PrettyLogger` do not relate to the contextual-logger change. They are harmless, but they add noise to a plugin-logging PR. Consider splitting them out.

findings.title: Middleware order and trace ID carry over correctly
findings.description: Verified by reading: the chain order is `Tracing → Metrics → ContextualLogger → Logger`, so the logger middleware receives a context that already holds the contextual attributes. `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` reads them through the provider registered in `init` (pkg/infra/log/log.go:55-61). The `traceID` field that the old `LoggerMiddleware` added explicitly is now supplied by the provider registered in `tracing.ProvideService` (pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91-97). That constructor is wired in `pkg/server/wire.go:249`. Both changed `plog.Logger` implementers (`TestLogger` and `grafanaInfraLogWrapper`) implement `FromContext`. A search of `pkg/` found no other type that implements `plog.Logger`.
